item.title: Yield Excitement Reaching Local Extreme?: 3-Minutes MLIV
item.description: Guy Johnson, Tom Mackenzie, Skylar Montgomery Koning and Mark Cudmore break down today's key themes for analysts and investors on "Bloomberg: The Opening Trade." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rising Yields Threaten to Puncture Asia’s AI-Driven Stock Rally
item.description: A rapid climb in Treasury yields is emerging as one of the biggest risks to Asia’s AI-driven stock rally, an uneasy link that highlights technology firms’ vulnerability to elevated borrowing costs.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Vishnoi and Winnie Hsu

item.title: US Stock-Index Futures Drop as Bond Yields and Oil Prices Rise
item.description: US stock-index futures fell as rising bond yields and a spike in oil prices unnerved investors.
item.dc:creator: Levin Stamm

item.title: Trump Rejects Iran Truce as War Escalates | Horizons Middle East & Africa 8/18/2026
item.description: Horizons Middle East & Africa is your daily spotlight on one of the world's fastest-growing regions. Live from Dubai, we bring you the latest global markets and analysis, plus news-making interviews, with a special focus on MEA. All that and more, as you head to the office in the Gulf, pause for lunch in Hong Kong, or start your day in London or Johannesburg. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ashley Boosts His Real Estate Empire With Harvey Nichols
item.description: Retail billionaire Mike Ashley's purchase of department store Harvey Nichols, situated in London’s exclusive Knightsbridge district, has given his company one of the best located stores in the UK. A Bloomberg analysis of property records shows that Frasers Group now owns around 8 million square feet of retail park and shopping center space, part of what the company’s CEO Michael Murray said is a 16 million-square-foot portfolio worth £2 billion ($2.7 billion). Bloomberg's Maddie Parker has more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How Vitol Won Exclusive Fuel Deals to Dominate Africa
item.description: Exclusive agreements to supply fuel to at least five countries have put Vitol Group, the world’s largest commodity trader, in an unusually powerful position as the dominant supplier to southern and East Africa — a region that relies almost entirely on imports of fuel to keep cars, trucks, tractors and boats running. Bloomberg's Jack Farchy reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Braskem’s Mexico Unit Files for Chapter 11 Bankruptcy in US
item.description: Mexico’s Braskem Idesa SAPI, a joint venture between Brazil’s Braskem SA and the conglomerate of Mexican tycoon Carlos Slim, has filed for bankruptcy protection as mounting financial strain and a worsening liquidity crunch weigh on the company.
item.dc:creator: Dorothy Ma and Giovanna Bellotti Azevedo

item.title: Bridgewater China Withstands July Rout That Left Quants Reeling
item.description: Macro hedge funds in China including Bridgewater Associates LP’s local unit emerged from the July selloff bruised but not defeated, holding on to their annual gains after a wild stock market selloff that pushed other funds into the red.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: AI Boom, Debt Surge Fuel Long Bond Pain | Insight with Haslinda Amin 8/18/2026
item.description: Insight with Haslinda Amin, a daily news program featuring in-depth, high-profile interviews and analysis to give viewers the complete picture on the stories that matter. The show features prominent leaders spanning the worlds of business, finance, politics and culture. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: FTSE 100 Outperforms as Oil Stocks Rise - Live Updates
item.dc:creator: Morwenna Coniam and Kit Rees

item.title: Maniatis: Oman Spill Cleanup May Cost USD 200-500M
item.description: Specialists are racing to salvage a sinking shadow-fleet tanker off Oman that has caused a massive oil slick. Personnel have already boarded the Caroline Bezengi, a Suezmax that has grounded off Oman’s southern coast. Dimitris Maniatis, CEO of maritime risk management firm Marisks spoke to Bloomberg’s Abeer Abu Omar on Horizons Middle East & Africa on the short & long-term consequences of such a spill. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Asian Bonds Follow Treasuries Lower on Concerns Over Government Finances | The Asia Trade 8/18/2026
item.description: "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade" brings you everything you need to know to get ahead as the trading day begins in Asia. Bloomberg TV is live from Sydney with Paul Allen, getting insight and analysis from newsmakers and industry leaders on the biggest stories shaping global markets. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: NSE Said to Seek Up to $55 Billion Valuation in Record India IPO
item.description: National Stock Exchange of India Ltd., the operator of the world’s largest derivatives exchange by trading volume, is seeking a valuation of as much as 5.26 trillion rupees ($55 billion) in its planned initial public offering, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Mascarenhas

item.title: Bond Slump Sends Long-Term Debt Costs to Highest in Decades
item.description: Longer-maturity bonds are at the epicenter of investor angst about everything from inflation to the debt-laden artificial-intelligence boom — and governments are paying the price.
item.dc:creator: Greg Ritchie and Matthew Burgess

item.title: Situational Awareness Sold Taiyo Yuden Shares to Citadel
item.description: Situational Awareness sold shares in Japan’s Taiyo Yuden Co. to Citadel and other investors when it offloaded part of its stake this month, it said in a filing.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Hilton and Aya Wagatsuma

item.title: Japan Five-Year Bond Sale Draws Strongest Demand Since June 2025
item.description: Japan’s five-year government bond auction Tuesday saw the strongest demand since June 2025, as a global rout in long-term debt spurred demand for shorter maturities.
item.dc:creator: John Cheng

item.title: Indian Rupee, Bond Bets Retreat as Dollar Swap Window Ends Early
item.description: Caught off-guard by India’s decision to close early a special window to draw foreign-currency deposits, traders are now paring bets on gains in the rupee and short-term bonds.
item.dc:creator: Subhadip Sircar and Pratigya Vajpayee

item.title: Hedge Fund Tax Break Grips Hong Kong as Banks Fear Exodus
item.description: Hong Kong’s move to cut taxes for hedge funds has set off a frenzied wave of maneuvering across the city’s financial sector, with investment banks fearing an exodus of prop traders and one fund even considering rebranding a receptionist as an investor relations official to make the most of the potential windfall.
item.dc:creator: Echo Wong, Eunice Xu, Bei Hu and Denise Wee

item.title: Stocks Fall as Bond Selloff Drives Risk Aversion: Markets Wrap
item.description: Stocks fell as long-dated bond yields pushed further into multidecade highs and oil prices extended their climb, draining traders’ appetite for risky assets.
item.dc:creator: Andre Janse van Vuuren

item.title: MCX Plans India Coal, Ore Exchanges to Boost Price Discovery
item.description: Multi Commodity Exchange of India Ltd. plans to invest as much as 2 billion rupees ($21 million) to start coal and minerals trading platforms as the government opens up the sectors to improve price discovery and transparency in the domestic market.
item.dc:creator: Preeti Soni
